text: Nib's commander. Go back to the Far Side, to the Ninth Wall before it fell: nine towers, and a black tide of faceless monsters climbing toward them. Nib is its last scout.
The commander's order: hold the gate until the army is through the pass. Then they'll come back for him. Yes, commander.
A young scout, Kett, begs Nib to come with him. Nib hands him a sealed message instead: go first, Kett. I'll be right behind you.
Kett runs, clutching the message, looking back the whole way.
Then, from a fortress far away, a bell rings the retreat.
And Nib holds the gatehouse alone as they pour over the wall.
One scratch in the stone for every day. He holds that gate for nine days.
Then he looks down the pass. The road is empty. Nobody comes back for him.
Back in the boss room, the knight raises its sword over them, and Jaeha shouts the obvious order. Nib, take its legs!
Nib lowers his knives. No. Not him. He won't.
Jaeha hauls him behind the pillar by the cloak, a hand's width ahead of the blade.
And the amber glow drains out of Nib's eye.
A window: field form has ended. Nib is back in rest form, and a summon in rest form cannot fight. Cooldown: one minute.
Nib won't look up. Leave him here, he mutters. He's useless for a minute.
Jaeha crouches to his level. Then he'll call him back in a minute. Everyone comes back. That's the rule.
Nib finally looks up at him.
The knight turns slowly in the hall, its red face sweeping the pillars like a searchlight.
But Jaeha is reading the floor: square plates with engraved borders, same as the corridor where his husk got shredded. And spike holes in the pillars.
Out comes the notebook. The plates by the side arch fire spikes from both pillars. The big centre plate drops the portcullis.
The plan, from above: the knight's path across the plates, and one small circle past the arch where somebody has to stand.
It always hits whatever is in front of it. So Jaeha will be in front.
Yerin grabs his sleeve. What is he doing? He can't fight that thing!
He won't fight it, he says, with a small grin. He's a trap-tester. He'll walk in first.
The notebook snaps shut. The plan is ready.
Then he strolls out across the open floor toward the arch, hands in his pockets.
Nib watches him go, knuckles tight on his knives.
He stops just past the arch and calls politely. Over here, sir. He's the only thing alive in front of it.
The knight charges straight at him across the plates.
Its iron foot comes down on the big centre plate. Click.
Spikes burst from both pillars and lock its legs.
Then the rusted portcullis slams down on its back, driving it to its knees.
The boss is pinned a metre from his face. Three hundred and twelve raids, sir. He knows a trap when he sees one.
Yerin's jaw drops. He trapped a boss. He actually trapped a boss.
But the gauntlets close on the bars, and the bars start to bend. Forty-one seconds of cooldown left.
It rams its helm into the bars, red light flaring in Jaeha's face.
So he shouts to Yerin: light up your hands as bright as you can, then hide!
Yerin steps out, and her palms blaze mint-white across the hall.
Something bright and alive. The knight twists toward it and swings blindly at her pillar.
The sword bites the stone a hand's width above her head.
Jaeha bangs on the bars to pull it back. Hey, sir! Still right here!
Yerin yells across the hall: is this what he does every single day?
Jaeha, sweating, gives her a thumbs-up. Usually there's less screaming.
Nib watches a small orange figure stand in front of a giant, so the others don't have to. A scout's job.
Then the spikes snap, one after another, and the bars bow. Three seconds.
The knight tears the whole portcullis out of the arch and knocks Jaeha flat.
Flat on his back, Jaeha sees the window he needs. Cooldown zero. Nib can take field form again.
Nib, come back! A cyan circle flashes under him, and the amber floods back into his eyes.
He looks across the hall at Jaeha. You called me back.
Jaeha grins up from the dust. He told him. Everyone comes back.
And a window: Nib answered a second call by choice. Seal two of five. His power doubles, from twenty percent to forty.
The seal breaks, and the Ninth Wall's colours flood back into his cloak, with the nine-tower sigil at his throat.
The knight's sword comes down on Jaeha, and Nib catches it on crossed knives. This time, his feet don't slide an inch.
He looks back over his shoulder: I still won't kill him. But I'll hold him for you.
That's all Jaeha needs. Hold him, and he'll find the way.
Then, deep in the empty helm, the red light flickers and turns a cold, pale white.
The knight stops pushing and leans down until its helm is level with Nib's face.
And out of that hole comes a voice, deep and clear. Nib...
Nib's pupil shrinks to a dot.
Jaeha stares up from the floor. It can talk?
The light steadies, and the voice says it again. End it, Nib. End it.
Before the Hush takes you too.
